title: Homepage copy leads with the pain in plain words: 'Your agents forget. Hunch remembers.'
context: David asked (2026-10-18) to make the homepage copy understandable and a banger, via the Don't Make Me Think lens. The old hero ('Give every agent a shared record to work from') was abstract, and its lede made visitors choose between two products (engineering memory vs self-hosted state server) before they knew what Hunch was.
decision: Hero H1 is 'Your agents forget. / Hunch remembers.' The lede names what is kept (what was decided, what got done, what's still owed — with sources, in Git) and the payoff (the next agent picks up where the last one left off). Section headlines are short claims ('AI reads your code. It wasn't there when you decided.', 'Don't trust the agent. Read the receipt.'). Jargon is gone from the body copy (partition, key-bound credentials, integration, supported rules). Honesty qualifiers stay: advice by default, strict mode blocks only where allowed, delivery depends on the assistant, unverified stays unverified. All five locales were regenerated from tooling/generate-site-locales.mjs.
consequences: README top and the npm description no longer share the site's sentence set (dec_327dbd3c78 consequence); align them in a follow-up
Hebrew/Russian/Arabic/Spanish translations were written by agents; a native read is still pending
alternatives_rejected: Keep the 'shared record' hero: abstract, and fails Krug's 5-second scan test
Two-product lede (coding memory OR state server): forces a choice before the visitor understands the product
Drop the honesty qualifiers to make it punchier: spends credibility; dec_327dbd3c78 requires only verifiable claims
